answer: Each identity locks 80 credits in a delta ledger and files one signed voyage log. Its delta is public, and its nadir, the voyage's lowest score, must clear a floor. Any auditor can replay it; a missing checkpoint, reused hash, or nadir below the floor burns the bond. A rented-voyage ring fails: a copied log keeps the original key and nadir timestamp, so both bonds burn. Each fake pays 120, 80 locked plus 40 fee; the thousandth pays 120, and 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 and pay 40,000, since each voyage needs a fresh route. An honest identity pays 40 once and recovers 80 after a clean epoch.
